dedupe_keys.name: ala seismic fragility formulations for water systems including buried pipeline vulnerability functions 2001

description: This April 2001 guideline of the American Lifelines Alliance, a public-private partnership of FEMA and the American Society of Civil Engineers, sets out seismic fragility formulations for water systems. The principal investigator was John M. Eidinger of G&E Engineering Systems, with contributors from Contra Costa Water District, EQE International, the San Francisco utilities, UC Berkeley, East Bay Municipal Utility District, Cornell University and Geomatrix Consultants, and the report was reviewed by engineers, academics and utility staff. It defines vulnerability and fragility relationships between component damage and hazard intensity and addresses inventory, uncertainty and randomness. Its buried pipeline section covers the factors that damage buried pipes, a wave propagation damage database with vulnerability functions (bin medians and 16th, 50th and 84th percentile functions) and the effect of permanent ground deformation, alongside other water system components. Coverage: US water utility experience. Format and access: a public 104-page PDF. Licence and cost: free. Caveats: written for water systems in 2001, so newer pipe data and later formulations are not included. Its buried pipe vulnerability functions can feed hazard exposure, resilience and cascading failure models of pipelines. It relates to Hazus, QGIS-EPANET and the BGS gas pipeline geohazard case in the catalogue.
